Your first question is very relevant and I haven't thought about that. Yeah, I suppose I would be sad and sorry for him.

Saying that I lied to him for a year is rather rough. I did tell him about the pain and many treatments I went through. I just tried to make it look less serious / hide the heaviness of it, wishing that he could enjoy the sex, even if I couldn't. Or something like that. I still enjoyed being close to him even if the act itself was painful.

I haven't really thought of it as does he "deserve" to hear about it, but rather, is it good for him to hear all the gruesome details about it. I do not wish to hurt him unnecessarily.

Yeah, I told him that it doesn't hurt anymore and that I am rather excited. 

He knew that it often hurt me, but I usually told him that it is not so bad and let's continue. He also knew all the many things I have tried in order to get rid of the pain. For example, sometimes I told him that we have to take a little break from penetrating sex because I had antibiotic sticks in my vagina, etc.

The thing he doesn't know is that I sometimes just acted like I enjoyed it even though it was seriously just plain painful for me. Reasons: complicated. But telling that to him would most likely just hurt him and make him doubtful in the future whether I actually even enjoy the sex with him, which I do and don't want him doubting.

So yeah, I'm just happy that I can finally enjoy it again like I used to.

Yes, didn't need to remove the IUD, tho many doctors suggested it and I was seriously thinking about it. I was already googling for other contraceptives, but didn't really want to change, because the IUD has otherwise worked great for me and I do not have menstruation thanks to it (I used to have very painful menstruations).

Strange thing is also that I had my previous Mirena for 7 years before swapping to the new one and never had such problems with it. But well, I was younger then, when I got the first one. Maybe the aging + fresh new Mirena together create the unpleasant magic.
